# Security Policy

## Security Announcements
Security fixes will be announced by posting them in the [security changelog](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/whats-new/security-changelog/).

## Scope and Supported Versions

The following versions of ClickHouse server are currently being supported with security updates:
"

clickhouse-local --query "
SELECT
    y::String || '.' || (y < toYear(today()) - 2000 - 1 ? '*' : m::String) AS Version,
    (n <= 3 OR (is_lts AND lts_n <= 2)) ? '✔️' : '❌' AS Supported
FROM
(
    SELECT
        y,
        m,
        count() OVER (ORDER BY y DESC, m DESC) AS n,
        m IN (3, 8) AS is_lts,
        countIf(is_lts) OVER (ORDER BY y DESC, m DESC) AS lts_n
    FROM
    (
        WITH
            extractGroups(version, 'v(\\d+).(\\d+)') AS v,
            v[1]::UInt8 AS y,
            v[2]::UInt8 AS m
        SELECT
            y,
            m
        FROM file('$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../list-versions/version_date.tsv', TSV, 'version String, date String')

            m DESC

)
LIMIT 1 BY Version

A public disclosure date is negotiated by the ClickHouse maintainers and the bug submitter. We prefer to fully disclose the bug as soon as possible once a user mitigation is available. title: Add changelog for 22.10
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A ClickHouse user or operator upgrading to version 22.10 needs a consolidated release changelog that explains what changed in that release.


  ## Desired outcome

  The 22.10 changelog should be published as a complete release summary so upgraders can review notable changes, fixes, and operational considerations in one place.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The 22.10 release notes are available as documentation, and they describe the release without changing any server behavior or product APIs.

  '
=== 22-11-changelog ===
title: Add changelog for 22.11
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Release readers use the 22.11 changelog to understand what changed in that line and to plan upgrades or feature adoption.

  ## Desired outcome

  Keep ClickHouse runtime behavior unchanged while polishing the 22.11 release notes so feature descriptions, terminology, and upgrade notes are accurate and readable.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The published 22.11 changelog reads like a coherent release document that users can trust when comparing versions.

  '
=== changelog-22-12 ===
title: Add changelog for 22.12
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  ClickHouse users and operators read the stable release changelog to understand what shipped in version `22.12`. This PR is a release-documentation update rather than a feature or behavior change.


  ## Desired outcome

  The `22.12` changelog should be added so readers can review the release summary in the standard project format. No runtime behavior, settings, or SQL semantics should change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The changelog file for `22.12` exists with the expected release notes, and the server product surface remains untouched.'
=== changelog-maintenance ===
title: Continue updating the changelog
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Operators and users read the project changelog and security policy generator output as the public record of what changed in a release, so those release notes need to stay accurate and well phrased.

  ## Desired outcome

  Refresh the published changelog text and supporting generation logic so the release notes describe the shipped features and fixes clearly, using correct names and corrected wording where the current text is misleading.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The release notes present the intended entries with corrected terminology and the generated security/version documentation stays internally consistent with the updated release narrative.

  '
=== changelog-navigation-cleanup ===
title: Update CHANGELOG.md
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The top-level changelog page is a navigation entry point for users reading release notes, so small formatting and anchor mistakes make the published documentation feel broken.

  ## Desired outcome

  Clean up the changelog table of contents and anchors so release navigation renders correctly and consistently in the published docs.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Readers can use the changelog page without broken line-break formatting or mismatched anchors, and no release content is lost in the cleanup.

  '
=== changelog-single-quote-default ===
title: Update CHANGELOG.md
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Upgrade notes are part of the operator contract for a database release, especially when defaults change in a way that can alter query parsing or output handling.

  ## Desired outcome

  Make sure the top-level changelog explicitly calls out the default change for `format_csv_allow_single_quotes` so operators can notice the compatibility impact during upgrade planning.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The upgrade notes include this default-change guidance in the public changelog, giving administrators a clear place to discover the new behavior.

  '
=== changelog-spelling-allowlist ===
title: add changelogs
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  The ClickHouse changelog and spelling workflow need to recognize newly introduced product terms so release notes can be published cleanly. This PR only updates internal documentation tooling data.


  ## Desired outcome

  The spelling allowlist should include the new changelog vocabulary without altering any server features, SQL syntax, or runtime behavior. This is maintenance for release documentation quality, not a user-facing product change.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The new term is accepted by the changelog and style tooling, and no ClickHouse query, setting, API, or operator workflow changes as a result.'
=== changelog-tags-workflow ===
title: Update README.md
category: docs
requirement: 'ClickHouse maintainers generating release notes should not have changelog tooling fail just because their local clone does not yet have tags fetched. The documented workflow for changelog.py should explicitly include git fetch --tags so the script runs successfully in a fresh or partial clone. This is a tooling and documentation fix with no server behavior change.

  '
=== changelog-version-refresh ===
title: Changelogs and versions
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Release managers and operators rely on changelog pages and version-date listings to understand which stable and LTS builds are available across maintained branches.

  ## Desired outcome

  The published release metadata should be refreshed so the documented version history remains accurate after the latest round of releases.

  ## Acceptance signals

  The affected changelog pages and `version_date.tsv` entries are updated consistently, and no server or client runtime behavior changes as part of this work.

  '
=== latest-release-changelogs ===
title: Generate missed changelogs for latest releases
category: test
requirement: '## Context

  Users reading release notes expect each published stable or LTS release to have a corresponding changelog page, and release managers need those pages in place for versions that were already shipped.


  ## Desired outcome

  Generate the missing changelog documents for the affected recent releases so the documentation set matches what was actually published.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The missing release-note pages now exist for the targeted versions, and version-to-date metadata is filled in so those releases appear complete in the documentation.

  '
